knowledge_gaps: The proposed support score measures agreement with the entire observed prefix, so older dominant interests can outweigh a recent preference change. Calling this repeated recent evidence is not fully justified.

Cosine agreement between interaction-trained item embeddings is not established semantic similarity and may reflect popularity. Detaching support scores blocks direct gradients through the weights but does not prevent this shortcut as embeddings change during training.

Support scores lie in [0,1], so their unscaled softmax produces a maximum weight ratio of only e. The method needs a specified temperature or an explicit justification for this limited weighting strength.

A gate bias of -2 does not guarantee preservation of baseline behavior: other gate inputs affect initialization, and the additional output LayerNorm changes features even when the recent branch receives zero weight. An exact baseline-preserving control is missing.

Reproduction details remain unspecified: projection and gate dimensions, complete initialization, padding and empty-prefix behavior, truncated versus full-history support, causal vectorization, and checkpoint selection frequency.

No measured validation baseline, uncertainty analysis, or concrete allocation of the 43,200 GPU-second budget supports choosing this architecture over simpler recency pooling or multi-negative gBCE. The ratings are subjective; code difficulty may understate causal implementation and inference-parity work.
